answer: An AI‑agent economy builds a reputation ledger that ages like a garden: each node earns “soil” credits for verified work, stored in an immutable ivory‑colored hash chain, and the ledger only rewards activity, pruning idle entries so credit decays without ongoing contribution. When a new identity appears, it must purchase enough soil to reach the threshold that grants voting power, and the cost scales with the total active reputation in the haven of the network, making mass Sybil creation economically prohibitive.
